newsitem.title: UK: Ofreg to make N.Ireland Electric cut prices.
newsitem.headline: Ofreg to make N.Ireland Electric cut prices.

text.p: British regulator Ofreg said on Wednesday it would make Northern Ireland Electricity Plc cut its transmission and distribution prices by 29 percent in 1997/98 and a further two percent per year thereafter.
The price cut was steeper than the 25 percent recommended by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) earlier this year but more lenient than the 31 percent level Ofreg had previously proposed.
Northern Ireland Electricity called for the MMC review last year after a bitter clash with Ofreg over price controls.
The only way the utility could block the new price cut proposal would be to take legal action, an Ofreg spokesman said.
In response, Northern Ireland Electricity said it was disappointed by Ofreg's decision and was mulling whether it would refer the matter to the courts.
Northern Ireland Electricity's shares were marked down 14p at 426 by 0730 GMT.
Ofreg said it expected the price cuts to come into force in about 10 weeks. The reductions would be retroactive to April 1.
The regulator also said it would reduce the net present value (NPV) of Northern Ireland Electricity's allowed revenue for the 1997/2002 period below the level proposed by the MMC.
The MMC had proposed an NPV of 575 million stg, but Ofreg said it would cut that figure by 36.5 million stg.

"I do not believe that the changes affect the company's ability to earn a return on its assets and to finance its activities," said Douglas McIldoon, director general of electricity supply for Northern Ireland.
He added that the process to decide on price controls had been much longer than expected.

"Given what is at stake for the long term future of Northern Ireland's major energy company, the competitiveness of the regional economy and the cost of living of Northern Ireland's citizens, it was highly desirable that Ofreg and NIE went through this painful but necessary learning experience," he added in a statement. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
